turns.response_html:
That carpet definitely looks like it’s seen better days—it has that classic "high-traffic grime" look, especially near the baseboards. Since you're dealing with an apartment, you'll want to be effective without losing your security deposit.

Here is a game plan to get that floor looking (and feeling) human-grade again:

1. The Deep Clean (Rent a Pro-Grade Machine)

Vacuuming won't reach the oils and dirt trapped in the fibers.

  • Rent a Carpet Cleaner: Go to a local hardware or grocery store (like Hy-Vee or Home Depot) and rent a Rug Doctor or Bissell Big Green.
  • The Secret Sauce: Don't just use the soap. Do a second pass with plain hot water and a splash of white vinegar. This removes the soap residue, which otherwise acts like a magnet for new dirt.

2. Targeted Spot Treatment

For those darker patches and mystery spots:

  • Enzymatic Cleaners: If any of that "disgusting" factor is organic (pets, food), use an enzyme cleaner like Rocco & Roxie or Nature’s Miracle. It breaks down the proteins rather than just masking them.
  • The Iron Trick: For stubborn wax or deep-set stains, lay a damp white towel over the spot and run a clothes iron (on low steam) over it. The heat can pull the stain up into the towel.

3. Texture Revival

After cleaning, older carpets often stay "matted" and crunchy.

  • Carpet Rake: Once the carpet is damp from cleaning, use a carpet rake (or even a stiff-bristled push broom) to pull the fibers back up. This helps it dry faster and restores that "fluff."

Apartment Living Pro-Tip

Document everything. Since you just mentioned it's "disgusting," make sure you have high-resolution photos of the carpet in its current state. Send them to your landlord now so you aren't charged for "damages" when you eventually move out.

turns.response_html:
In Iowa, landlords are required to maintain a safe and sanitary environment. If the carpet is simply ugly or worn ("ordinary wear and tear"), they aren't legally forced to replace it, but you have a much stronger case if it’s a health hazard.

How to push for replacement:

  • Check for Health/Safety Hazards: If the carpet has mold, a permanent foul odor, or is fraying enough to be a trip hazard, mention these specifically. Landlords are more likely to act when "liability" or "inhabitability" is mentioned.
  • The "Tripping" Strategy: If the carpet is loose or bunched up, send a written notice stating it is a safety risk. Under Iowa law, landlords generally have 7 days to address repairs after receiving written notice.
  • Negotiate a Renewal: If your lease is up soon, tell them you'll sign for another year only if the carpet is replaced. This is often the most successful tactic in Ames' competitive rental market.
  • Involve an Inspector: If the landlord ignores you and the carpet is truly unsanitary (e.g., active mold), you can contact the City of Ames Rental Inspector. They can "cite" unsanitary conditions, forcing the landlord to remove or clean it within 30 days.

Document everything. Take clear photos and send your requests via email or certified mail so you have a paper trail.

For issues with unsanitary rental conditions, you can contact the Ames City Inspection division directly.

  • Email: inspections@cityofames.org
  • Phone: 515-239-5153
  • Location: 515 Clark Ave, Unit 205, Ames, IA 50010
  • Office Hours: Monday–Friday, 7:30 AM – 4:30 PM

The Inspections Division is responsible for enforcing the Ames Rental Housing Code and ensuring properties meet safety and sanitation standards. You can request to speak with a Building Official or a Rental Housing Inspector regarding your situation.

In Iowa, mold qualifies as a health and safety violation if it makes the unit "uninhabitable" or unsanitary. Generally, it must be visible growth or a persistent musty odor that indicates moisture issues.

While Iowa doesn't have specific "mold levels" in its legal code, the Ames Rental Housing Code requires landlords to keep premises free from dampness to prevent health hazards. If you see fuzzy patches—typically black, green, or white—or if the carpet feels damp and smells "earthy," it likely qualifies for an inspection.

Next Steps:

  • Document it: Take close-up photos of the growth.
  • Test it: Buy a mold test kit from a hardware store for immediate proof.
  • Report it: Call the inspection office listed above to schedule a walkthrough.

turns.response_html:
Several local stores in the Ames area carry home mold testing kits, typically in the hardware or safety sections.

Local Stores in Ames

You can find these kits at major home improvement centers nearby:

  • The Home Depot: Typically stocks multiple options including Mold Armor and My Mold Detective.
  • Lowe's Home Improvement: Often carries PRO-LAB and My Mold Detective kits.
  • Ace Hardware: Generally carries the Pro Lab Mold Test Kit in their safety and security department.
  • Target: Occasionally stocks the Safe Home Premium Mold Test Kit in their home or pharmacy sections.

Recommended Mold Test Kits

If you are deciding between different types, here are a few highly-rated options that provide different levels of detail:

The Mold Armor FG500 DIY Mold Test Kit is an affordable "first step" option. It allows for at-home testing with visible results in 48 hours and offers a mail-in lab analysis for more specific identification.

  • Methods: Supports HVAC, airborne, and surface testing.
  • Pros: Very affordable and easy to use for a quick "yes/no" answer.

The My Mold Detective Mold Test Kit is a more professional-grade choice if you are concerned about air quality. Unlike simple petri dish tests, it uses a reusable air sampling pump to capture spores more accurately.

  • Methods: Specialized for professional-style air sampling.
  • Pros: Reliable technology used by industry experts; includes easy-to-follow instructions.

The Pro Lab Mold Test Kit MO109 is another common DIY choice. It is widely available at hardware stores and provides an optional lab analysis to determine exactly which mold species are present.

  • Methods: Visual sampling, HVAC air sampling, and settling plate.
  • Pros: Inexpensive entry point with a pre-paid return mailer for lab testing.

For the most reliable results, especially if you plan to present this to a landlord, I recommend choosing a kit that offers AIHA-accredited lab analysis. This provides a formal report rather than just a subjective "petri dish" observation.
